definitions.gloss: Dear Sir/Madam, To Whom It May Concern
definitions.explanation: A formal salutation used at the beginning of a Japanese letter. It is always paired with the closing salutation 敬具 (けいぐ, "Yours sincerely") at the end of the letter.

examples.japanese: {拝啓|はいけい}　{時下|じか}⟦ますます→ますます：01604_masumasu⟧ご{清祥|せいしょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こととお{慶|よろこ}び⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧。
examples.english: Dear Sir/Madam, I trust you are doing well.
examples.notes: A standard formal letter opening combining {拝啓|はいけい} with a seasonal greeting.

examples.japanese: {拝啓|はいけい}　⟦{初春|しょしゅん}→初春：21709_shoshun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{候|こう}、⟦{皆様|みなさま}→皆様：15860_minasama⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お{変|か}わり⟦なく→ない：01118_nai⟧お⟦{過|す}ごし→過ごす：02062_sugosu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こと⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{存|ぞん}じます→存じる：05912_zonjiru⟧。
examples.english: Dear Sir/Madam, as the new year begins, I hope everyone is doing well.
examples.notes: An example with a seasonal reference ({時候|じこう}の{挨拶|あいさつ}).

examples.japanese: ⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{書|か}き{出|だ}し→書き出し：19293_kakidashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「{拝啓|はいけい}」⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{始|はじ}め、「⟦{敬具|けいぐ}→敬具：12977_keigu⟧」⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{結|むす}ぶ→結ぶ：02308_musubu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{正式|せいしき}→正式：03376_seishiki⟧な⟦マナー→マナー：11139_manaa⟧だ。
examples.english: Proper etiquette is to begin a letter with "haikei" and close it with "keigu."

notes:
{拝啓|はいけい} literally means "humbly stating" ({拝|はい} = humbly + {啓|けい} = to state/inform). It is the standard formal opening for Japanese letters and must always be paired with the closing ⟦{敬具|けいぐ}→敬具：12977_keigu⟧ ("respectfully concluded").

FORMAT: In a Japanese letter, {拝啓|はいけい} is followed by a space (full-width) and then a seasonal greeting ({時候|じこう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{挨拶|あいさつ}→挨拶：02505_aisatsu⟧). The body of the letter follows, and the letter ends with ⟦{敬具|けいぐ}→敬具：12977_keigu⟧.

OTHER LETTER OPENINGS:
- ⟦{謹啓|きんけい}→謹啓：22309_kinkei⟧: more formal than {拝啓|はいけい} (paired with {謹白|きんぱく} or ⟦{敬白|けいはく}→敬白：22308_keihaku⟧)
- {前略|ぜんりゃく}: "dispensing with formalities" — used when skipping the seasonal greeting (paired with {草々|そうそう})

NOTE: {拝啓|はいけい} is used in formal business letters, official correspondence, and ceremonial writing. It is not used in casual emails or messages.
